youtube.aciklama: When we speak, we also hear our own voice; this auditory feedback plays an important role in controlling speech. When we hear our own voice with a delay of about 200 milliseconds, the fluency of speech is clearly disrupted. In a noisy place, we also raise our voice without noticing; this is called the Lombard effect.
